newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to quiz Lisbon and Athens on low-sulphur diesel.
newsitem.headline: EU to quiz Lisbon and Athens on low-sulphur diesel.

text.p: The European Commission is to ask Athens and Lisbon about their implementation of new EU diesel rules after reports that sales of banned fuel in those countries were due to continue past the October 1 deadline.
"Letters are expected to go out soon," Commission spokesman Jesper Jorgensen told Reuters on Tuesday.
The letters, which Jorgensen said should go this week, will ask the Greek and Portuguese governments to report on the market situation in their countries.
The action came after market reports that sales were to continue in these markets despite an October deadline for halting sales of diesel containing more than 0.05 percent sulphur.
"Clearly, according to the press reports, the situation is not legal," Jorgensen said.

Portugese state oil company Petrogal said on Monday that it would continue to distribute the higher-sulphur diesel. A company statement said the Economy Ministry's Directorate-General for the Environment and Energy had allowed them to do so.

A Commission official said on Monday the EU executive had received no requests from EU governments for waivers to the 1993 rules. In any case, such waivers were permitted only in times of supply crises, the official added.

Mediterranean oil traders said on Monday that Portuguese and Greek refiners had won temporary deferrals of the deadline, specifying that Portuguese state oil company Petrogal and Greece's Public Petroleum Corp had waivers until March 1997 and January 1997 respectively.
One Italian trader said that even on the day before the deadline, Petrogal was in the market looking for the higher-sulphur fuel.
